title: Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the importance of protecting nature
content:

                28 JUL 2026 7:48AM by PIB Delhi The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, said that the welfare of humanity lies in the protection and respect of nature. He noted that India’s timeless traditions also inspire us to uphold this righteous way of life and live in harmony with the natural world. The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam- “लोकपालाश्च ते सर्वे वासवप्रमुखास्तथा। ऋतवः षट् च ते सर्वे मासाः संवत्सराः क्षपाः॥ दिनानि च मुहूर्ताश्च स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु ते सदा। श्रुतिः स्मृतिश्च धर्मश्च पातु त्वां पुत्र सर्वतः॥” The Subhashitam conveys that alife lived in harmony with nature and righteousness is the foundation of happiness, security, and well-being. Therefore, may the guardians of the directions, the principal deities led by Indra, the six seasons, all months, years, nights, days, and auspicious moments always bring blessings and prosperity. May the Vedas, sacred traditions, and righteousness also protect everyone in every way and at all times. title: Ministry of Civil Aviation inaugurates Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Amritsar
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Civil Aviation Ministry of Civil Aviation inaugurates Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Amritsar Amritsar becomes the second spoke airport under India's International Aviation Hub Strategy प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 JUL 2026 11:00AM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Civil Aviation today inaugurated Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Amritsar, making it the second airport in the country to be integrated into India's pioneering Hub & Spoke framework for international passenger movement. The inauguration marks the next phase of the Government's strategy to transform India into a global aviation hub by providing seamless international connectivity to passengers from across the country through Indian hub airports. The launch follows the successful commencement of India's first Hub & Spoke operations from Varanasi on 25 June 2026. Over the past one month, the system has operated smoothly, demonstrating the operational viability of the model and receiving an encouraging response from passengers. During this period, passengers originating from Varanasi have been seamlessly connected through Delhi to eighteen international destinations, validating the effectiveness of the initiative in simplifying international travel. Through a video message congratulating all the stakeholders present at the Amritsar airport, Union Minister of Civil Aviation Ram Mohan Naidu said, ““Hub & Spoke is not merely an aviation model; it is an opportunity model. Delhi will serve as the hub, while Amritsar will emerge as a major international gateway for Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh. With its strong diaspora connections and vast regional catchment, Amritsar is among the Indian cities that stand to benefit the most from this transformation in global connectivity.” Amritsar occupies a unique position as one of India's major international gateways, serving pilgrims, members of the Indian diaspora, business travellers and tourists from Punjab and neighbouring regions. Its inclusion under the Hub & Spoke framework is expected to substantially improve access to global destinations through Indian hubs while providing passengers with a faster, more convenient and predictable travel experience. Emphasizing the larger national vision, the Minister added , “Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, India is working towards building its own globally competitive aviation hubs. This is not only about improving passenger convenience; it is about strengthening India’s aviation sovereignty and ensuring that Indian hubs connect India to the world.” Beyond improving passenger experience, the initiative is expected to generate wider economic benefits by strengthening tourism, trade, investment and regional development. Studies undertaken by the Ministry indicate that the development of aviation hub operations could generate nearly 0.4 million direct and indirect jobs and contribute an additional USD 30 billion to India's economy by 2030. By 2047, the cumulative impact is projected to support approximately 16 million direct and indirect jobs while contributing nearly USD 1.4 trillion to the national economy. With the commencement of operations from Amritsar, international passengers can now complete check-in, immigration and customs formalities at Amritsar before departure. Their baggage will be checked through to the final international destination, enabling them to transfer seamlessly at the designated hub airport to their onward international flight without undergoing immigration or customs formalities again. Highlighting the transformational impact of the Hub & Spoke model on international connectivity from Amritsar, the Minister said: “Until now, passengers travelling from Amritsar had direct international connectivity to only seven destinations. With the introduction of the Hub & Spoke model, the global connectivity of Delhi Airport will effectively become available to passengers right from Amritsar itself. Travelers will be able to access more than 20 international destinations with a single check-in and a single baggage tag, making the entire journey far more seamless. At present, nearly 1.5 lakh passengers travel from Amritsar to Delhi every year to board international flights, while another 1.5 lakh passengers arrive from overseas via Delhi to reach Amritsar. As travel becomes significantly easier under this integrated system, we expect passenger traffic to grow rapidly.” The airlines have estimated a potential of nearly 250 passengers per day from Amritsar alone to benefit from the Hub & Spoke model through Delhi. As additional spoke airports are brought under the framework in the coming months, the next phase is expected to facilitate approximately 1,200 passengers every day, equivalent to nearly 4.5 lakh passengers annually, thereby significantly expanding seamless international connectivity from regional India. The initiative significantly enhances passenger convenience while maintaining the highest standards of security, facilitation and regulatory compliance. The Hub & Spoke framework forms a key pillar of the Government's International Aviation Hub Strategy, which seeks to strengthen Indian airports as preferred gateways for international travel, improve network efficiency for Indian carriers and reduce dependence on overseas transit hubs. By leveraging India's strategic geographical location and expanding airport infrastructure, the initiative aims to retain a larger share of international transfer traffic within the country while enhancing the competitiveness of India's aviation sector. The inauguration of Hub & Spoke operations from Amritsar marks another significant milestone in the phased rollout of India's International Aviation Hub Strategy. Additional spoke airports are at advanced stages of operational readiness and will be integrated into the network in a phased manner, creating a nationwide system of seamless international connectivity through Indian hub airports. The initiative represents an important step towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 by building a more connected, efficient and globally competitive aviation ecosystem. The event was graced by Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Shri Puneet Kansal, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Shri Vipin Kumar, Chairman, Airports Authority of India; Shri Sharad Kumar, Chief Advisor, AAI; Shri P. Balaji, Group Head – Governance, Air India; representatives from the Bureau of Immigration, Customs and CISF. The occasion also witnessed the presence of a wide spectrum of industry associations, hotel and hospitality stakeholders, travel partners, tourism representatives and other key aviation and trade stakeholders, reflecting the strong collaborative support for strengthening international connectivity from Amritsar. *** Divyanshu Kumar (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2290234) आगंतुक पटल  : 29 Ministry of Civil Aviation Ministry of Civil Aviation inaugurates Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Amritsar Amritsar becomes the second spoke airport under India's International Aviation Hub Strategy प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: India Leads the Wilderness in Tiger Conservation
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder India Leads the Wilderness in Tiger Conservation “Protecting Tigers, Preserving Ecosystems” Posted On:
                28 JUL 2026 11:01AM by PIB Delhi India has emerged as a global leader in tiger conservation through science based policies and strong institutional support. The country is now home to nearly 70% of the world's wild tigers. Technology driven monitoring, effective governance and community participation have strengthened conservation outcomes. India is also advancing global cooperation to secure the future of tigers and their habitats. Thriving Tigers, Resilient Ecosystems International Tiger Day, observed every year on 29 July , highlights the global importance of tiger conservation. For India, it reaffirms the Government's long-standing commitment to science-based conservation and sustainable development. The day also showcases India's remarkable conservation achievements. Today, India is home to the world's largest wild tiger population , accounting for nearly 70% of all wild tigers globally . This success reflects decades of sustained policy support, scientific management and community participation, positioning India as a global leader in tiger conservation. This achievement is rooted in India's deep cultural and ecological connection with the tiger. For centuries, ancient coins, royal seals and temple carvings have portrayed the tiger as a symbol of strength and sovereignty. Recognising this enduring legacy, the Government declared the Royal Bengal Tiger as the National Animal in 1972 . Today, the tiger continues to represent India's rich biodiversity, ecological wealth and shared natural heritage across diverse landscapes. Beyond its cultural significance, the tiger plays a vital ecological role. As an apex predator and umbrella species, it helps maintain healthy forest ecosystems. Conserving tiger habitats protects forests, rivers and countless other species. These forests regulate water, conserve soil, support pollination and moderate local climates. They also reduce disaster risks and provide ecosystem services that sustain rural livelihoods and urban economies. By protecting tigers and their habitats, the Government is strengthening biodiversity conservation, enhancing ecological security and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat through sustainable development. Did You Know? International Tiger Day traces its origins to the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit held in November 2010 . Leaders from 13 tiger-range countries, including India, adopted the ambitious Tx2 goal to double the global wild tiger population by 2022. Today, it serves as a global platform to review conservation progress, strengthen international cooperation and raise awareness. In 2010, only about 3,200 wild tigers were estimated to remain globally. By 2022, improved conservation and scientific monitoring increased the estimate to around 4,500, with a plausible range of 3,700–5,600 tigers. According to recent global estimates, approximately 5,711 wild tigers remain worldwide, representing an increase of around 78% since 2010. Rise in the Tiger Numbers: From Crisis to Recovery India's tiger conservation efforts have emerged as a global model of wildlife recovery. The country has more than doubled its scientifically assessed tiger population since 2006. The All India Tiger Estimation (2022) places India's tiger population at 3,682 . The 2022 All India Tiger Estimation covered 20 States and surveyed over 6.41 lakh kilometres on foot. It is among the world's largest and most comprehensive wildlife assessments. This remarkable recovery reflects sustained policy support, science-based conservation and strong institutional governance. Long-term habitat protection, rigorous monitoring and coordinated implementation continue to strengthen tiger conservation across India. Robust Governance Architecture for Tiger Conservation India’s policy framework for tiger conservation combines long term vision with sustained institutional support at national and state levels. Project Tiger, the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and Tiger Conservation Plans together provide a robust, science based governance architecture for tiger habitats. Project Tiger Project Tiger is a flagship Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Government of India. It is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). The scheme aims to secure viable tiger populations in their natural habitats. It provides financial and technical assistance to tiger range States for conservation efforts. The programme combines habitat protection, scientific management and regular field based monitoring. This approach has strengthened conservation measures over time. According to the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) Report (2023) , Project Tiger has established a network of 58 tiger reserves across 18 tiger-range States . These reserves cover around 84,500 square kilometres , which is about 2.56% of India's geographical area . Today, Project Tiger remains a cornerstone of India's wildlife conservation efforts and reflects the Government's long term commitment to protecting tigers and their habitats. Did You Know? Section 38 V (3) of the Wildlife Protection Act, (WPA), 1972 requires every State Government to prepare a Tiger Conservation Plan for each tiger reserve. Such plans must ensure protection of tiger reserves and provide habitat inputs to maintain viable populations of tigers, co predators and prey animals National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) NTCA oversees the implementation of Project Tiger and related conservation initiatives. NTCA provides scientific, technical and financial guidance to tiger range States. It approves Tiger Conservation Plans and issues standard operating procedures for reserve management. The Authority also monitors the management of tiger reserves through periodic assessments. Its science based approach improve habitat protection, improves conservation outcomes and supports the long term survival of wild tigers across India. Did You Know? NTCA is chaired by the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It also includes Members of Parliament, senior government officials and experts. The Authority guides tiger conservation, oversees tiger reserves and ensures effective implementation of Project Tiger across the country. Tiger Task Force The Government of India constituted the Tiger Task Force to re-examine conservation policies and recommend reforms. The Tiger Task Force reviewed India's tiger conservation framework and recommended key policy reforms. It brought together administrative experts, ecologists and community representatives. The Task Force emphasised transparency, community participation and stronger institutional support for Project Tiger . Its recommendations shaped a more robust conservation framework. They led to significant amendments to the Wildlife (Protection) Act in 2006 . The amendments established the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) as statutory bodies. India's tiger conservation framework reflects a strong governance model built on institutions and cooperative federalism. This integrated approach is helping secure the future of tigers while advancing India's biodiversity. Did You Know? India's tiger reserves follow a landscape-based conservation approach . Each reserve includes a Core Area (also known as Critical Tiger Habitat) and a Buffer Area . Core Areas receive the highest level of protection. Buffer Areas balance conservation with sustainable livelihoods. Also, Wildlife corridors connect tiger reserves, enabling safe movement and maintaining healthy tiger populations across landscapes. Monitoring and Evaluation of Tigers in India India has developed a robust, science-based system to monitor and evaluate its tiger population. The approach combines field surveys, camera traps, digital technologies and scientific analysis. It generates reliable data on tiger populations, prey species and habitat quality. This information guides evidence-based conservation planning and adaptive management. Continuous monitoring strengthens habitat protection and enables informed management decisions across tiger landscapes. All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) : The World's Largest Biodiversity Survey AITE is the world's largest biodiversity survey. Conducted every four years, it is led by the NTCA in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) . It estimates tiger populations, co-predators, prey species and habitat quality across all tiger bearing States. The 2022 assessment also included India's first nationwide survey of ungulates. The exercise highlighted the importance of healthy prey populations for sustaining viable tiger populations. Did You Know? The All India Tiger Estimation is recognised as the world's largest biodiversity survey . The NTCA's camera trap survey also holds a Guinness World Record as the world's largest camera trap wildlife survey. Together, advanced technologies and scientific monitoring make India's tiger estimation among the most rigorous in the world. Technology Driven Monitoring India has integrated advanced digital technologies into every stage of tiger monitoring.  The Monitoring System for Tigers – Intensive Protection and Ecological Status (M-STrIPES) uses GPS, GPRS and remote sensing technologies for field monitoring. GPS tagged photographs improve data accuracy and reduce human error. The platform integrates field observations into a central database for scientific analysis and informed decision making. Artificial intelligence further strengthens monitoring. The Camera Trap Data Repository and Analysis Tool (CaTRAT) automatically classify camera trap images by species. ExtractCompare identifies individual tigers using their unique stripe patterns. Collectively, these tools improve the accuracy and reliability of tiger population estimates. Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) The MEE assesses how well tiger reserves are managed. The framework evaluates planning, protection, management processes and conservation outcomes. It helps identify management gaps and reinforce accountability. By 2022 , 51 tiger reserves had been evaluated under the framework. Twelve reserves received "Excellent" ratings, while the average management score reached 78% . The findings guide policy decisions, strengthen reserve management and support long-term conservation planning. India's Global Leadership in Tiger Conservation India is actively collaborating with countries across the world to strengthen tiger and wildlife conservation. Key partnerships include transboundary biodiversity conservation with Nepal and Bhutan . Collaboration with Myanmar focuses on combating timber trafficking and conserving tigers and other wildlife. India also cooperates with Russia on camera trap data management and through the Indo-Russia Working Sub-Group on Tiger and Leopard Conservation. Partnerships with Botswana, South Africa, Guatemala, Cambodia, Kenya and Namibia strengthen wildlife conservation, management and sustainable biodiversity use. India has also established bilateral cooperation with China on tiger conservation. These partnerships reinforce India's commitment to global wildlife conservation through science, cooperation and shared action. International Big Cat Alliance ( IBCA) IBCA is a global coalition of 95 big cat range and partner countries , scientific organisations and conservation partners. The Alliance promotes cooperation for conserving seven big cats —tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. The Union Cabinet approved its establishment on 12 March 2024 , with its Secretariat headquartered in India . Building on India's globally recognised tiger conservation experience, the IBCA strengthens international collaboration to protect big cats and their habitats. Global Tiger Forum (GTF) GTF is the world's only intergovernmental organisation dedicated exclusively to tiger conservation. Headquartered in New Delhi , it brings together 13 tiger range countries -Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam. The Forum promotes a common approach to conserving tigers, their prey and habitats. It supports landscape-scale conservation, regional capacity building and technological innovation to strengthen tiger conservation across member countries. Through knowledge sharing and international cooperation, the GTF reinforces India's leadership in global tiger conservation. Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme (ITHCP) ITHCP is the International Union for Conservation of Nature's (IUCN) flagship tiger conservation initiative. It is funded by the German Government through KfW Development Bank. The programme supports science-based conservation projects across priority tiger landscapes in Asia. It promotes habitat protection, landscape level conservation and international collaboration. India actively participates in ITHCP programmes, strengthening regional efforts to conserve tigers and their habitats. Did You Know? Conservation Assured Tiger Standards CA|TS is a global certification system that ensures effective management specifically of tiger conservation areas. Launched at the 1st Asian Parks Congress in Japan in 2013 . It sets benchmarks for protection, habitat management, community involvement, and wildlife monitoring. CA|TS supports efforts to create safe, sustainable environments for tigers and preserve global biodiversity. CA|TS has accredited 23 Indian tiger reserves ensuring global best practices in conservation . India's international partnerships are strengthening collective action for tiger conservation across borders. By sharing knowledge, technology and best practices, India continues to advance global efforts to protect tigers and their habitats. Thriving Tigers, Resilient Ecosystems International Tiger Day, observed every year on 29 July , highlights the global importance of tiger conservation. For India, it reaffirms the Government's long-standing commitment to science-based conservation and sustainable development. The day also showcases India's remarkable conservation achievements. Today, India is home to the world's largest wild tiger population , accounting for nearly 70% of all wild tigers globally . This success reflects decades of sustained policy support, scientific management and community participation, positioning India as a global leader in tiger conservation. This achievement is rooted in India's deep cultural and ecological connection with the tiger. For centuries, ancient coins, royal seals and temple carvings have portrayed the tiger as a symbol of strength and sovereignty. Recognising this enduring legacy, the Government declared the Royal Bengal Tiger as the National Animal in 1972 . Today, the tiger continues to represent India's rich biodiversity, ecological wealth and shared natural heritage across diverse landscapes. Beyond its cultural significance, the tiger plays a vital ecological role. As an apex predator and umbrella species, it helps maintain healthy forest ecosystems. Conserving tiger habitats protects forests, rivers and countless other species. These forests regulate water, conserve soil, support pollination and moderate local climates. They also reduce disaster risks and provide ecosystem services that sustain rural livelihoods and urban economies. By protecting tigers and their habitats, the Government is strengthening biodiversity conservation, enhancing ecological security and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat through sustainable development. Did You Know? International Tiger Day traces its origins to the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit held in November 2010 . Leaders from 13 tiger-range countries, including India, adopted the ambitious Tx2 goal to double the global wild tiger population by 2022. Today, it serves as a global platform to review conservation progress, strengthen international cooperation and raise awareness. In 2010, only about 3,200 wild tigers were estimated to remain globally. By 2022, improved conservation and scientific monitoring increased the estimate to around 4,500, with a plausible range of 3,700–5,600 tigers. According to recent global estimates, approximately 5,711 wild tigers remain worldwide, representing an increase of around 78% since 2010. Rise in the Tiger Numbers: From Crisis to Recovery India's tiger conservation efforts have emerged as a global model of wildlife recovery. The country has more than doubled its scientifically assessed tiger population since 2006. The All India Tiger Estimation (2022) places India's tiger population at 3,682 . The 2022 All India Tiger Estimation covered 20 States and surveyed over 6.41 lakh kilometres on foot. It is among the world's largest and most comprehensive wildlife assessments. This remarkable recovery reflects sustained policy support, science-based conservation and strong institutional governance. Long-term habitat protection, rigorous monitoring and coordinated implementation continue to strengthen tiger conservation across India. Robust Governance Architecture for Tiger Conservation India’s policy framework for tiger conservation combines long term vision with sustained institutional support at national and state levels. Project Tiger, the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and Tiger Conservation Plans together provide a robust, science based governance architecture for tiger habitats. Project Tiger Project Tiger is a flagship Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Government of India. It is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). The scheme aims to secure viable tiger populations in their natural habitats. It provides financial and technical assistance to tiger range States for conservation efforts. The programme combines habitat protection, scientific management and regular field based monitoring. This approach has strengthened conservation measures over time. According to the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) Report (2023) , Project Tiger has established a network of 58 tiger reserves across 18 tiger-range States . These reserves cover around 84,500 square kilometres , which is about 2.56% of India's geographical area . Today, Project Tiger remains a cornerstone of India's wildlife conservation efforts and reflects the Government's long term commitment to protecting tigers and their habitats. Did You Know? Section 38 V (3) of the Wildlife Protection Act, (WPA), 1972 requires every State Government to prepare a Tiger Conservation Plan for each tiger reserve. Such plans must ensure protection of tiger reserves and provide habitat inputs to maintain viable populations of tigers, co predators and prey animals National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) NTCA oversees the implementation of Project Tiger and related conservation initiatives. NTCA provides scientific, technical and financial guidance to tiger range States. It approves Tiger Conservation Plans and issues standard operating procedures for reserve management. The Authority also monitors the management of tiger reserves through periodic assessments. Its science based approach improve habitat protection, improves conservation outcomes and supports the long term survival of wild tigers across India. Did You Know? NTCA is chaired by the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It also includes Members of Parliament, senior government officials and experts. The Authority guides tiger conservation, oversees tiger reserves and ensures effective implementation of Project Tiger across the country. Tiger Task Force The Government of India constituted the Tiger Task Force to re-examine conservation policies and recommend reforms. The Tiger Task Force reviewed India's tiger conservation framework and recommended key policy reforms. It brought together administrative experts, ecologists and community representatives. The Task Force emphasised transparency, community participation and stronger institutional support for Project Tiger . Its recommendations shaped a more robust conservation framework. They led to significant amendments to the Wildlife (Protection) Act in 2006 . The amendments established the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) as statutory bodies. India's tiger conservation framework reflects a strong governance model built on institutions and cooperative federalism. This integrated approach is helping secure the future of tigers while advancing India's biodiversity. Did You Know? India's tiger reserves follow a landscape-based conservation approach . Each reserve includes a Core Area (also known as Critical Tiger Habitat) and a Buffer Area . Core Areas receive the highest level of protection. Buffer Areas balance conservation with sustainable livelihoods. Also, Wildlife corridors connect tiger reserves, enabling safe movement and maintaining healthy tiger populations across landscapes. Monitoring and Evaluation of Tigers in India India has developed a robust, science-based system to monitor and evaluate its tiger population. The approach combines field surveys, camera traps, digital technologies and scientific analysis. It generates reliable data on tiger populations, prey species and habitat quality. This information guides evidence-based conservation planning and adaptive management. Continuous monitoring strengthens habitat protection and enables informed management decisions across tiger landscapes. All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) : The World's Largest Biodiversity Survey AITE is the world's largest biodiversity survey. Conducted every four years, it is led by the NTCA in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) . It estimates tiger populations, co-predators, prey species and habitat quality across all tiger bearing States. The 2022 assessment also included India's first nationwide survey of ungulates. The exercise highlighted the importance of healthy prey populations for sustaining viable tiger populations. Did You Know? The All India Tiger Estimation is recognised as the world's largest biodiversity survey . The NTCA's camera trap survey also holds a Guinness World Record as the world's largest camera trap wildlife survey. Together, advanced technologies and scientific monitoring make India's tiger estimation among the most rigorous in the world. Technology Driven Monitoring India has integrated advanced digital technologies into every stage of tiger monitoring.  The Monitoring System for Tigers – Intensive Protection and Ecological Status (M-STrIPES) uses GPS, GPRS and remote sensing technologies for field monitoring. GPS tagged photographs improve data accuracy and reduce human error. The platform integrates field observations into a central database for scientific analysis and informed decision making. Artificial intelligence further strengthens monitoring. The Camera Trap Data Repository and Analysis Tool (CaTRAT) automatically classify camera trap images by species. ExtractCompare identifies individual tigers using their unique stripe patterns. Collectively, these tools improve the accuracy and reliability of tiger population estimates. Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) The MEE assesses how well tiger reserves are managed. The framework evaluates planning, protection, management processes and conservation outcomes. It helps identify management gaps and reinforce accountability. By 2022 , 51 tiger reserves had been evaluated under the framework. Twelve reserves received "Excellent" ratings, while the average management score reached 78% . The findings guide policy decisions, strengthen reserve management and support long-term conservation planning.
